spec.prompt: Close exterior shot at the open outer end of the inflatable Volga airlock tube (the pale fabric cylinder with a round metal rim and a hinged hatch lid, third reference) in orbit. the cosmonaut Alexei Leonov (face and suit exactly as in the first two reference images), in a ballooned, over-inflated, rigid white Berkut suit puffed tight like a balloon, tries to get back in: his swollen suit is wedged in the round rim, shoulders and chest too wide for the opening. He grips the rim with both stiff gloves, pushes, strains, twists his shoulders, backs out a little and pushes again, and still cannot fit; his knees and elbows barely bend. The white umbilical tether floats behind him. Camera close and slightly above, the rim and his helmet clearly readable; the upper third of the frame is empty black space, the blue Earth at the bottom. Photorealistic, shot on 35mm film, IMAX documentary realism in the spirit of Apollo 11 (2019) and Gravity. Accurate 1965 Soviet hardware: the white Berkut spacesuit with rust-orange harness straps, a white helmet with red CCCP letters above the visor, Soviet markings only. Hard directional sunlight, deep black space, crisp silhouettes. No on-screen text, no captions.
